quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Why do motorcyclists often move into another lane while taking a curve?
questions.explanation: If you enter a curve or turn too fast, you may cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's space cushion should:

options.text: Not be necessary in most situations.
Be avoided to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle needs longer to stop, the pavement is slippery, you cannot see ahead clearly, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, use both brakes:

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the best stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you during turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control, and hold onto handholds or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Motorcycle windshields:

options.text: Do not protect your eyes from the wind.
Protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look at the road directly in front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn toward where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn toward where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward your destination. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab the rear brake.
Press down on the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when stopping.

questions.question: Engine braking is:

options.text: Slowing down by turning the engine off.
Not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle like braking. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs show road rules like speed limits. They are rectangular and white with black letters or symbols. Riders must follow these signs.

questions.question: Many factors affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which one does NOT affect it?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Your height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Rain suits should:

options.text: Not be needed because motorcycles should not ride in rain

questions.explanation: Good rain suits for motorcycles do not tear or puff up at high speeds.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Ride one foot behind the vehicle in front of you
Signal only when you want to
Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay alert and be ready to avoid a crash
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turns, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best for groups. But riders should switch to single-file through curves, turns, and when entering or leaving highways.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when it is warm outside?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot
Yes, but take breaks to cool off
Yes, riding jackets keep you cool even in warm weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets keep you cool even in warm weather
questions.explanation: Riding jackets protect you and help prevent dehydration in warm weather. Many are designed to keep riders cool even in heat.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, it is usually best to:

options.text: Shift your weight toward the good tire
Brake on the good tire and steer to the roadside
Use both brakes and stop quickly

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the roadside
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip both handlegrips firmly. Ease off the throttle and go straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the good tire. As you slow down, move to the roadside, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Motorcyclists in a group should avoid riding in pairs because:

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders
Helmet reflections may make it hard for riders to see
Pairs do not give riders enough space to avoid hazards
Left-side riders cannot exit highways easily

questions.correctAnswerText: Pairs do not give riders enough space to avoid hazards
questions.explanation: Never ride in pairs. Each rider needs enough room to maneuver and avoid hazards.

questions.question: When securing a load, you should place it:

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low. Putting them high, like on a sissy bar, raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Distribute weight evenly on both sides to avoid pulling the bike to one side.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.question: The best lane position depends on:

options.text: Always staying in the right portion of the lane.
Always staying in the center portion of the lane.
Always staying in the left portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What best reduces head and neck injuries in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to prevent head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Adjust them so you can see the lane behind you and the lane next to you.

questions.question: What increases your visibility to other drivers?

options.text: Turning off your headlight during the day.
Keeping your headlight on at all times.
Riding in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright and reflective clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and change your lane position based on conditions.
